title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: S a scheme with p·1_S = 0, f: X → S, and E an O_X-module with an integrable connection relative to S. The page continues §3 of a draft on Picard-type sheaves of modules with connection: P^{ci}_{X/S} for invertible modules with integrable connection, and P^{cip} ⊂ P^{ci} for those whose p-curvature also vanishes.

(1) The opening question. Can one define, for any E with integrable connection and without assuming a local p-basis, a p-curvature tensor K ∈ Γ(X, End(E) ⊗ (Ω^1_{X/S})^{⊗p})? In modern terms this is the Cartier–Katz p-curvature ψ(D) = ∇(D)^p − ∇(D^{[p]}). It is additive and p-linear in D, so it is naturally a section of End(E) ⊗ F*Ω^1. Grothendieck's (Ω^1)^{⊗p} stands for this p-linear (Frobenius-twisted) target. The point of the question is generality: what replaces it when X/S is not smooth or has no p-basis.

(2) Exact sequence (3.2), rank one. Let Pic^{ci}_{X/S} be the image of P^{ci} → Pic_{X/S}, i.e. invertible sheaves that locally admit an integrable connection. A connection on O_X is d + ω with ω closed. Gauge change by a unit u replaces ω by ω + du/u. The p-curvature of d + ω is K_0(ω) = ω^{⊗p} − F^*_{X/S}(C̃ω), formula (3.3), where C is the Cartier operator. This is Katz's formula ψ(d+ω) = F*(ω^{(p)} − Cω).

This gives a complex, named the 'faisceau de Cartier' Cart_{X/S}: f_*O_X^* --dlog--> f_*Z^1_{X/S} --K_0--> f_*(Ω^1)^{⊗p}. Its middle cohomology is the 'défaut d'exactitude dans le milieu'. It maps to P^{ci0} (connections whose p-curvature vanishes, on trivialisable bundles). Then P^{ci0} → Pic^{ci} → f_*(Ω^{⊗p}) / Im K_0. The last map sends a line bundle to the class of the p-curvature of any local connection on it.

The NB records that K_0 is additive but not O-linear: it is a p-linear part ω ↦ ω^p minus a p^{-1}-linear part (Cartier).

(3) Cartier descent. Assume a local p-basis. A connection with zero curvature and zero p-curvature on a quasi-coherent E is the same as a Λ-module structure, where Λ = O_S[O_X^p] ≅ O_{X^{(p/S)}}/J and J = Ker(O_{X^{(p/S)}} → F_{X/S*}O_X). Equivalently it is a quasi-coherent module on the ringed space (X^{p/S}!) := (X, Λ). Hence P^{cip}_{X/S} is the sheaf associated to S' ↦ Pic(X_{S'}^{p/S'}!).

The next page draws the consequences. When X/S is smooth, X^{p/S}! = X^{(p/S)}, so P^{cip} ≅ Pic_{X^{(p)}/S} ≅ Pic^{(p)}_{X/S}. The forgetful map P^{cip} → Pic is F_{X/S}^*, which is the Verschiebung of Pic. Combining with (3.3) gives Ker(V_Pic) ≅ {closed forms with Cω = ω} modulo dlog of units. Grothendieck notes that V would have to be defined in sufficient generality for this to make sense.

Purpose: a 'Picard scheme with connection' framework that links Gauss–Manin/Cartier material to the Frobenius and Verschiebung of Pic, and later to comparison with the Albanese.
errors: Notation (Ω^1)^{⊗p}: the p-curvature really lives in End(E) ⊗ F*_{abs}Ω^1 (p-linear forms), not in the literal O-linear tensor power. In the rank-one case ω ↦ ω^{⊗p} only makes sense read as p-linear; this is a notational looseness, not a mathematical error.

The sequence (3.2) is sketched without stating its exactness hypotheses, beyond the parenthetical remark that the bracketed complex is not exact in the middle. The leftmost arrow and the precise meaning of P^{ci0} are left vague.

The identification of P^{cip} with a Picard functor of (X, O_S[O_X^p]) presupposes the local p-basis/Cartier descent equivalence. Without a p-basis, this ringed space need not reproduce the category of modules with zero curvature and zero p-curvature. That is exactly the gap behind the opening question.

ideas.what: p-curvature of an integrable connection in characteristic p, and the question of defining it without a p-basis
ideas.usually_credited_to: Cartier (unpublished); Katz, 'Nilpotent connections and the monodromy theorem' (1970)

ideas.what: p-curvature of the rank-one connection d+ω equals ω^p − F*(Cω), additive but not linear
ideas.modern_name: Katz's formula for the p-curvature of rank-one connections (Cartier operator)

ideas.what: Exact sequence relating Picard of line bundles with integrable connection, dlog, and the Cartier operator ('faisceau de Cartier')
ideas.modern_name: Pic^♮ / Picard functor with connection; dlog–Cartier complex
ideas.usually_credited_to: Mazur–Messing (1974) for the universal extension and Pic^♮; Milne/Illusie for dlog–Cartier sequences

ideas.what: Cartier descent: connections with zero curvature and zero p-curvature correspond to modules over O_S[O_X^p], hence P^{cip} = Pic of the ringed space (X, O_S[O_X^p])
The forgetful map P^{cip} → Pic is F*_{X/S}, i.e. the Verschiebung of Pic; Ker V_Pic ≅ Cartier-fixed closed 1-forms modulo dlog
ideas.modern_name: Verschiebung of the Picard scheme; logarithmic forms (Cω = ω) and Frobenius/Verschiebung kernels

missed.claim: Grothendieck asks for a p-curvature theory for integrable connections on X/S in full generality (no local p-basis, non-smooth X). He proposes the ringed space (X, O_S[O_X^p]) ('X^{p/S}!') as the right Frobenius-descent object, with Picard functor P^{cip}. The next page adds that the Verschiebung of Pic would need definition in comparable generality.
missed.quote: Peut-on définir un tenseur p-courbure sur X, qui soit K∈Γ(X, End(E)⊗(Ω^1_{X/S})^{⊗p}) ?
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: p-curvature and Cartier descent for singular or non-smooth morphisms is still handled case by case (log structures, crystalline or stacky substitutes). The specific 'X^{p/S}!' approach seems not to have been developed, but this is a modest thread.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is essentially Katz's p-curvature formula for rank-one connections and Cartier descent. It also identifies F* on Pic with Verschiebung and gives the classical description of Ker V via Cartier-fixed forms, all of which appeared in Katz, Oda, Mazur–Messing and Milne around the same time. The packaging (Pic^{ci}, 'faisceau de Cartier', the ringed space X^{p/S}!) and the non-smooth question are mildly interesting but not novel.
transcription_corrections: The parenthetical above the bracketed complex reads '(défaut d'exactitude dans le milieu)', not '(défaut de courbure dans le monde)'.
'Idée[?] dans le cas...' should probably read 'Puis dans le cas de l'existence locale d'une p-base'.
'f^*_{X/S}(C̃ω)' in (3.3) is the pullback by the relative Frobenius F_{X/S}.
'on sait que les modules p.ex. E' is closer to 'on sait que pour les modules quasi-cohérents E sur X'.
The superscript on f_* in (3.2) is uncertain (fl / dR / tt); 'fl' (flat-sheafified direct image) fits the context best.
